how: Chicago Park District runs public archery ranges (e.g. Belmont Harbor and 72nd St) for first-timers and practiced shooters, and Archery Bow Range Chicago rents bows by the session.
Chicago Curling Club in Northbrook runs two-hour Learn2Curl sessions on its dedicated ice for adults, with no experience needed, October to March.
Movement (Lincoln Park and Wrigleyville), Brooklyn Boulders and First Ascent climbing gyms offer bouldering day passes with shoe rental.
Movement Lincoln Park, Brooklyn Boulders and First Ascent Avondale offer top-rope walls up to about 50-60 ft, and Maggie Daley Park has an outdoor climbing wall.
Chicago has an amateur cricket scene of about 100 teams in leagues such as the American Cricket Conference and Illinois Premier League Cricket Conference, with matches at Warren Park and elsewhere.
Lincoln Square Fencing teaches foil and sabre from beginner to elite, and Windy City Fencing and Illinois Fencers Club (Mt. Prospect) also run beginner classes.
Sail Chicago teaches adults on small keelboats from downtown harbors, and SailTime Chicago runs ASA courses from Burnham Harbor.
SailTime Chicago runs ASA 101-106 keelboat courses on 33-36 ft Hunters from Burnham Harbor, and Sail Chicago teaches Basic to Skipper Prep on small keelboats.
Urban Kayaks, Chicago Kayak and Kayak Chicago run lessons and tours on the Chicago River, Lake Michigan and Skokie Lagoons, including four-hour beginner classes.
Urban Kayaks, Chicago Paddle Company (Osterman Beach) and Chicago SUP offer beginner SUP lessons, yoga and rentals on the lakefront harbours.
Learn Scuba Chicago and Dive Right In Scuba run PADI/NAUI Open Water courses with pool sessions in Chicago-area pools and quarry checkout dives.
Maggie Daley Park has a quarter-mile ice skating ribbon with skate rental, open in winter.
Forest Preserves of Cook County maintain 13 trail systems (Des Plaines River Trail, Palos, Thorn Creek and others) for hiking.

how: Adler Planetarium's Doane Observatory has a 20-inch telescope, the largest available to the public in the Chicago area, with public viewing and Adler After Dark events.
The Second City Training Center runs Improv 1, Improv 1A and drop-in improv classes for beginners in Chicago.
The Second City offers a Stand-Up 1 course and open stages for testing stand-up material.
Old Town School of Folk Music teaches guitar, banjo and mandolin in group classes and private lessons, with instrument rentals available.

how: Evanston Art Center runs multi-week wheel-throwing courses, and Color Cocktail Factory (18th St, Pilsen) offers one-off beginner wheel sessions.
Evanston Art Center offers Pinch, Slab, Coil handbuilding courses and ceramic sculpture, and Color Cocktail Factory runs clay sculpting workshops.
Evanston Art Center runs 'Bookbinding: Basics & Beyond' and Chicago Botanic Garden offers a Botanical Covers bookbinding workshop.
Remade in Chicago holds screen printing workshops (BYO T-shirt) at its Logan Square studio.
The Paintbrush on N Clark St runs an Adult WaterColors class.
Popcraft on W Division St runs candle DIY classes.
Discovery Center (N Elston Ave) offers an Intro to Knitting class.
Discovery Center offers a six-session beginning tap dance class.
Dance Center Chicago on N Lincoln Ave runs Bachata 101 and Kizomba classes.
Tohkon Judo Academy, a non-profit dojo at the Japanese American Service Committee building, teaches Kodokan-style judo starting with breakfall training.
ChampYon TaeKwonDo USA Academy (since 1982) and Legacy TKD Academy run Olympic-style taekwondo classes with forms and sparring.
Chicago Lions Rugby Football Club (founded 1964, USA Rugby) plays in the Midwest Rugby Premiership.
Meetup lists Suburban Ultimate Frisbee (Schaumburg) and other Chicago-area ultimate pickup groups.
Meetup groups such as We Pickleball for Fun! and Cube Chicago Padel run recurring pickleball sessions in the city.
Cube Chicago Padel hosts padel and pickleball events and college nights listed on Meetup.
Chicago Park District runs free public skate parks (Grant Park Skate Park, Burnham 31st Street, Wilson Skatepark) for novice to advanced riders.

Grant Park's skate park is designed for skateboards, scooters, inline skates and BMX bikes, and Logan Boulevard Skate Park is shared by skaters and BMX riders (closed for expressway repairs at last check).
Blackhawks Ice Center, Fifth Third Arena and Morgan Park Sports Center run learn-to-play programs and adult leagues such as the Blackhawks Adult Hockey League, with some gear rental.
Figure Drawing Chicago and Studio 215 host drop-in and class figure drawing sessions with live models.
Meetup groups such as Chicago Gay Drink and Draw and Chicago Creative Collaborators hold regular sketching sessions.
Chicago Streets and Beyond Photography Group, Chicago Photography Community and West Suburban Photography Group run regular photo meetups.

how: Evanston Art Center runs a six-session Intro to Darkroom Photography covering black-and-white film development and gelatin silver prints.
Choral-Aires Chorus holds weekly Monday rehearsals in the Chicago area.
Dance Center Chicago teaches Intro, Beginner and Intermediate Argentine Tango in four-session courses for adults.
Lou Conte Dance Studio offers drop-in basic and beginning ballet for adults and teens, and Dance Dynamics runs Adult Ballet.
Circle Studio and Discovery Center in Chicago run one-day beginner stained glass workshops, and Evanston Art Center and Highland Park Art Center offer courses.
Evanston Art Center runs multi-week beginning jewelry and metalsmithing courses, and Chicago Jewelry and Lapidary Art School teaches wire-wrapping workshops.

Suburban stables such as Danada Equestrian Center (Wheaton), Double J Riding Club (Countryside) and Freedom Woods (Morton Grove) offer lessons from beginner level, and Cook County forest preserves have bridle trails.
Trinity Academy of Irish Dance (Southport Ave), McNulty School, Dennehy School and the Irish American Heritage Center teach Irish dance classes across Chicago and suburbs.
Ensemble Espanol Spanish Dance Theater, based at Northeastern Illinois University, teaches flamenco and Spanish dance and has operated for about 40 years.
Dance Center Chicago teaches Intro, Beginner and Intermediate Swing leading to Lindy Hop, and Big City Swing runs swing courses on W Randolph St.
Ausrine's Arts Room offers a leather surface design book cover class, and Evanston Art Center runs wet-formed leatherwork.
Linda Z's Sewing Center runs Embroidery for Newbies and machine embroidery classes; Chicago Botanic Garden and Evanston Art Center offer hand embroidery courses.
Evanston Art Center runs oil painting courses such as Painting the Still Life in Oils and Painting with Texture (oil and acrylic).
Evanston Art Center teaches Ohara Ryu ikebana in a five-session course, and Morton Arboretum has run ikebana workshops.
Chicago calligraphy classes (Evanston Art Center, Spudnik Press, Discovery Center) teach Western italic, brush and modern lettering; no Chinese calligraphy class was found on the listing.
Chicago Rowing Foundation (Clark Park Boathouse), Lincoln Park Boat Club and Chicago Rowing Union run learn-to-row sessions on the Chicago River.
Greater Chicago Dragon Boat Club runs beginner paddling sessions on the Chicago River with no experience or equipment needed.
Chicago Park District lists 13 stocked lagoons, 22 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline and nine harbors open for fishing year-round, with pier and parking passes for some sites.
Stocked lagoons in Chicago parks and Lake Michigan harbours and piers allow fishing for perch, trout and other freshwater species.
NeighborSpace holds land for community gardens across Chicago, with individual plots leased seasonally (e.g. 94 raised beds at the 62nd Street Garden in Woodlawn, $50 per full plot).
Meetup groups such as Chicago Hiking, Outdoors, & Social Group, Southwest Suburban Weekday Woods Walkers and Slow Walking, Meandering Mornings run guided walks at nature centers and forest preserves.
The Windy City .Wavs Producer's Meetup hosts regular beat and song feedback sessions for music producers.
The Chicago area is flat glacial plain with no natural crags; the nearest outdoor climbing is Devil's Lake, Wisconsin (about 3 hours' drive) or Wisconsin's Sauk Prairie.
No big walls exist in the flat Chicago area; the nearest are in the Rockies and Yosemite (a long flight away).
Mangroves need a subtropical coast; the nearest are in Florida, about a 2-hour flight from Chicago.
Lake Michigan has no meaningful tides, so there is no intertidal zone; the nearest tidal coast is the Atlantic seaboard, about a 2-hour flight away.
Ocean surfing is impossible on an inland lake; the nearest ocean waves are on the Atlantic or Gulf coasts, about a 2-3 hour flight from Chicago.
Camel racing is not practised in the Midwest; it is a Gulf and South Asian tradition (e.g. the UAE or Saudi Arabia).
Buzkashi is played in Central Asia (Afghanistan) and has no organised presence in Chicago.

how: The Cooper's Hill cheese-rolling event is held annually near Gloucester, England, and there is no Chicago equivalent.
Elephant polo requires elephants and is played in Nepal, Thailand and India; none are available in the Chicago area.
There is no bobsled track in the Chicago area; the nearest are Lake Placid, New York, and Park City, Utah.
PianoForte Piano Performance Meet Up holds regular piano meetups in Chicago, and online piano lessons are listed for the city.
